title: Why do technical writers provide captions for images and how to do it
metaTitle: Why do technical writers provide captions for images and alt text on Mac
description: Technical writers provide captions and alt text to ensure accessibility for all users and legal compliance. Learn why this task is difficult and how to fix it.
targetKeyword: why do technical writers provide captions for images
intro: Technical writers provide captions and alt text for images to ensure that information is available to all users regardless of their visual ability. This practice is essential for meeting Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and avoiding legal risks associated with non-compliant documentation.
tldr: Alt text makes your documentation accessible to screen readers.
Legal requirements for accessibility are becoming stricter every year.
Creating descriptions is time-consuming and prone to human error.
You can use a hybrid approach of AI drafting and human verification.

blocks.text: The challenge of image accessibility description generation

Writing effective alt text is more than describing what you see. It requires understanding the intent of the image within the context of your documentation. Technical writers often struggle to decide what information is redundant and what is essential for the reader to understand the product.
Why do technical writers provide captions for images and alt text

Beyond legal compliance, providing captions and alt text improves the overall quality of your work. It forces you to clarify your visual content and ensures that users who rely on assistive technology have the same experience as sighted users. When you provide clear descriptions, you reduce confusion and support a wider audience.

items: Better SEO for your documentation pages
Compliance with international standards like WCAG

blocks.text: Many writers treat alt text as an afterthought. This happens because the process is manual and slow. When you have dozens of screenshots to document, writing unique descriptions for each one feels like a burden. This leads to generic text that does not actually help the user.
How to fix your accessibility workflow without spending money

items: Use native accessibility checkers in Microsoft Word or PowerPoint via Review > Check Accessibility.
Create a simple Apple Shortcut that sends a screenshot to an AI service for a draft description.
Keep a style guide for image descriptions to ensure consistency across your team.
Review your images for redundancy; if the text already explains the image, use empty alt attributes where appropriate.

blocks.text: If you work in a regulated industry like law, medicine, or finance, always check your company guidelines before using external AI tools. Never upload sensitive or private client data to public AI services.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps with accessibility descriptions

Lazur helps you bridge the gap between drafting and verifying. You can use your voice to ask for descriptions of complex images on your screen. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the document.

faq.question: Is AI-generated alt text always accurate?
faq.answer: No. AI can identify objects but often misses the specific context or industry jargon required for technical documentation. Always review and edit AI-generated text.

faq.question: What is the difference between a caption and alt text?
faq.answer: A caption is visible to all users and provides extra context. Alt text is hidden from sighted users and is intended for screen readers to describe the image content.

costs.title: Legal Risk
costs.text: Non-compliance leads to lawsuits and expensive audits that can cost up to 30,000 dollars.

costs.title: Time Loss
costs.text: Manual writing of alt text for hundreds of images slows down your publishing cycle.

causes.title: Contextual Complexity
causes.text: It is difficult to determine what information in an image is already covered in the text.

causes.title: Workflow Bottlenecks
causes.text: Manual creation is tedious, causing writers to skip it when deadlines are tight.

fixes.title: Native Tools
fixes.text: Use the built-in accessibility checkers in Microsoft Office or Google Docs to find missing descriptions.

fixes.title: Hybrid Approach
fixes.text: Use AI to generate a first draft of the description and then refine it yourself for accuracy.
